### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/verify`, touching **49** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/verify/README.md`, `packages/verify/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**28** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e448d3c27f4bd9031428347f6bdd865445486497`.

⛔ **9** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/verify/README.md`, `packages/verify/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `organization_id (literal, 35 pages)`, `/data/:object (route, 67 pages)`
- **31** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **30** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e448d3c27f4bd9031428347f6bdd865445486497` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `2e84e8ac290602763b4ebda2b61eee23df1e2bc1` — the merge of head `9c89d3cc89a967ef9eb61627c02855d831a158ab` into base `e448d3c27f4bd9031428347f6bdd865445486497`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 2e84e8ac290602763b4ebda2b61eee23df1e2bc1 && git checkout 2e84e8ac290602763b4ebda2b61eee23df1e2bc1
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e448d3c27f4bd9031428347f6bdd865445486497 9c89d3cc89a967ef9eb61627c02855d831a158ab && git checkout -B drift-repro e448d3c27f4bd9031428347f6bdd865445486497 && git merge --no-ff 9c89d3cc89a967ef9eb61627c02855d831a158ab

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e448d3c27f4bd9031428347f6bdd865445486497
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs e448d3c27f4bd9031428347f6bdd865445486497` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `9c89d3cc89a967ef9eb61627c02855d831a158ab`
Local-runs: none

Read at 2026-10-12T16:13Z, adversarially, against AGENTS.md Prime Directives #10 and #12 and Post-Task Checklist step 3. Inputs: card #15953 (body and all 15 comments: the classification table `6115219467`, the slice 3 claim `6125131626`, the dev report `6127784027`, the seat's ACCEPT `6127885139` read as a claim, and slice 2's record `6118395322` on PR #22953 as the precedent); PR #23069 body, file list and the net diff of `refs/pull/23069/head` against merge base `0cbfb7c32c` (9 files, +1630 / -7); the check-runs on the head. Nothing was built, run or re-run; the only local commands were `git show` / `git diff` against the fetched ref and the record template print.

### ① Derived judgments

**The three functions and eleven types, reachable and coherent: right.** `packages/verify/package.json` maps `.` to `dist/index.js` / `dist/index.d.ts` (and the `require` pair), and `packages/verify/src/index.ts` exports `deriveUniqueScopeCases`, `runUniqueScopeProofs`, `formatUniqueScopeReport` and exactly the eleven types the changeset lists from `./unique-scope.js`, so every one is reachable through the published entry. Shapes mirror the family beside them: `deriveXCases(config)` / `runXProofs(stack, token, config, { doors? })` / `formatXReport(report)` is `deriveDeleteBehaviorCases` / `runDeleteBehaviorProofs` / `formatDeleteBehaviorReport` to the parameter; `app` is computed by the same expression as `delete-behavior.ts` and `reference-shape.ts`; `summary.hardFailures` is `contradicted + failed`, the gate count slice 2 introduced; the six field statuses are slice 2's vocabulary with each docblock matching `fieldStatus` and `judge` line for line. Three places where an export says slightly more than the code measures, none a contract defect: (a) `runUniqueScopeProofs` promises it "never throws on a per-field failure", but the `stack.rows` read-backs in `holder`, `offerInsert` and `offerUpdate` are not caught, so a harness-level read fault escapes rather than landing as `failed` (the same gap slice 2's record noted on its family); (b) `UniqueScopeCase.across` ("what a second holder in ANOTHER organization meets") is still emitted as `admitted` on a case whose across leg is excluded (a one-to-one reference, a `tenancy.tenantField` object), so the report carries an expectation beside the reason it is not measured; no verdict rests on it, since the leg never runs; (c) `boot.legs.within` is the literal `run` even when `options.doors` is empty. Noted, not flagged.

**`os verify --unique-scopes`: right.** `Flags.boolean` with `default: false`, typed into `runVerification`. With the flag, `bootStack(config, { multiTenant, hostRoot })` is a fresh stack stopped in `finally`, where `multiTenant` is the run's own `resolveVerifyMultiTenant(flags)` and `hostRoot` the same value the four sibling phases take; `uniqueScopes.summary.hardFailures` is added under `?? 0`; `uniqueScopes` rides `emitJson` (a `JSON.stringify`, so an `undefined` value emits no key); the text branch is `if (uniqueScopes)`. Without the flag nothing moves: `hardFailures` adds 0, the `--json` document carries no `uniqueScopes` key, stage 1 runs and exits exactly as before, and the exit status reads what it read. The only thing that moves for every caller is help text (the command `description` and one `examples` row), a widening the minor carries. `packages/cli/test/verify-unique-scopes.test.ts` spawns the real process and pins it (`'uniqueScopes' in doc` false and exit 0 without the flag; exit 0 on the proven app; exit 1 on the faulted door); `packages/cli`'s `test` script is a bare `vitest run`, so both its projects, the integration one included, run under CI's Test Core.

**The expectation's source: right, and every excluded shape is excluded, not modelled.** `deriveUniqueScopeCases` reads the scope from `FieldSchema.safeParse(def).data.unique` through `isUniqueDeclared` / `isGlobalUnique` and from nowhere else, so an `autonumber` that authors nothing carries the `'organization'` the spec's `.overwrite()` tail puts there, never a hand copy of that default. What each scope means is `UniqueScopeSchema`'s docblock and ADR-0120 D1 (per-organization: refused in the same organization, admitted in another; `'global'`: installation-wide). The organization column is `isTenancyDisabled` (ADR-0066); the wall is `postureEnforcesWall` over `stack.tenancy().posture` (ADR-0105). The refusal's identity is `DuplicateRecordError`'s documented split (`DUPLICATE_RECORD` thrown, `UNIQUE_VIOLATION` on every REST route per the 2026-09-03 ruling recorded in `protocol.ts`) and `field` only when `uniqueViolationColumn` named a column. The two shapes the brief asks about: for an object with no organization column, the cross-organization `refused` is read from the docblock's own sentence ("on an object with no tenant column at all (`tenancy.enabled: false`) both per-organization spellings degrade to the listed column alone") and ADR-0120 D1 / S11, a single-column index being installation-wide by construction, so published, not invented; for a one-to-one reference, the family states NO across expectation: `acrossExcluded` names the reason and the leg is never run, which is an exclusion, and the safe direction (the stale `across: 'admitted'` beside it is item (b) above). Also excluded or not-derivable with the reason, never given an expectation: a parse refusal, `formula` / `summary`, a closed value space, a multi-valued reference, an undeclared target, an unsynthesizable object, a `tenancy.tenantField` object, and the REST door on `readonly` / `system` / `id` / runtime-issued fields. A unique `indexes[]` entry is kept out of the population, and the README and changeset say so.

**Attribution: right on every named path, with one residual the seat owes a carrier (see ③).** `judge` credits `held` on a refusal only when the code is the door's unique code and the refusal's `object` is absent or the probed one; a refusal naming another field is `unattributed`; a field-less refusal on an insert is `unattributed` unless the twin was written; the twin is `create(second, c.object, { [c.field]: freshValue }, n)` with the SAME fixture counter `n` as the refused write, so only the probed value differs; an update changes only the probed field, so it needs no twin. A hook's own code (`DUPLICATE_VALUE`, the hotcrm shape), a rule, a permission, a constraint on another field (field named), and a field-less refusal the twin meets too (the `uqa_tagged` control) all stay out of `proven`, and the attribution control pins both halves. The residual: a declared unique COMPOSITE `indexes[]` entry that covers the probed column together with columns the fixtures hold constant (an optional field with a `defaultValue`, a hook-stamped value, a required type `vary` leaves alone such as a boolean) refuses the second holder field-less (a composite is `undefined` under `uniqueViolationColumn`'s contract) and admits the twin, and the update probe credits the same way. Both paths then credit a refusal the field's own declaration did not cause. It matters only when the field's own index is absent: on `os verify`'s fresh database that is an engine or driver fault, the class the family exists to find, masked by the author's composite; on a reused database it is the ADR-0120 D4 not-enforced state the driver logs at boot. R10 does not fence it: `lintUniqueDeclarations` is advisory (`severity: 'warning'`, "never fails a build") and reads single-column declared indexes only, composites exempt by design. The family already reads `indexes[]` (`uniqueFields`), so the tightening is cheap: on a field-less refusal where a unique `indexes[]` entry covers the probed column, report `unattributed`, or write a second twin varying that entry's other columns. Not a FAIL: the shape needs the author's own composite over the same column plus an unenforced field index, the docs state the mechanism exactly ("it names the field, or it names none and the same record with only the probed value changed is admitted"), every other refusal errs toward inconclusive, and nothing in this PR's evidence (fixture, controls, hotcrm as reported) carries that shape.

**The two `NOT_A_STAND_IN` rows: true of the code.** The gate's candidate is an exported function whose parameter 0 is annotated with an interface declared in the package and re-exported as a type from its index. `runUniqueScopeProofs(stack: VerifyStack, ...)` and `formatUniqueScopeReport(report: UniqueScopeReport)` are exactly those two; `deriveUniqueScopeCases(config: any)` is not a candidate. `VerifyStack` is the concrete handle `bootStack` returns and `UniqueScopeReport` is a value this package produced, so neither is a surface an out-of-tree implementer provides; the rows' words are the sibling rows' words. `Lint & Repo Gates`, which carries `check:verify-stand-in`, is green on the head.

**Docs and changeset sentences against the diff: right, two of them narrower than the code.** Changeset: the export list is the full set (3 functions, 11 types), the signature line is the real one, the refusal identities, the twin sentence, the exclusions and `hardFailures` all match `unique-scope.ts`. Its provisioning sentence, "the way a user makes one (a sign-up that creates its own)", compresses two calls into one phrase: `provisionOrganization` is `stack.signUp(email)` THEN `POST /auth/organization/create { name, slug }` THEN a check that the new organization is the sign-up's active one; the PR body names the route, the changeset does not. Accurate in substance, imprecise in the parenthetical; and the leg is also reported not run on a walled boot whose provisioning fails, a second reason the sentence does not name but the code reports on `boot.acrossNotRun`. README: "Five app-agnostic proof families", the bullet, the opt-in paragraph, the exit-code sentence, the status table (each row matches `fieldStatus` / `judge` / `deriveUniqueScopeCases`) and the API line all match. Its membership-policy sentence is grounded in this repo: `assertWalledMembershipPolicyDeclared` in `packages/plugins/organizations/src/membership-policy-gate.ts` throws `WalledMembershipPolicyError` on any non-`single` posture when an `auth` service is present and no policy is declared. The declaration may come from the `auth.membership_policy` setting OR `OS_AUTH_MEMBERSHIP_POLICY` (`plugin-auth.ts` names both); the README names the env var only, which is the practical route on a fresh `os verify` boot with no seeded settings. Accurate, slightly narrow. `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`: the example row, the paragraph in the `os verify` section only (insert and update, both doors, the attribution sentence, the across provisioning, the not-run reason, the autonumber parse default, the system-door-only rule, what fails the run, "inconclusive, never proven") and the `--json` key list (`uniqueScopes` with its `boot`) match `verify.ts` and the family.

**First-consumer evidence (hotcrm): consistent with the retired pins, as reported.** Rows 6 and 7's D halves proven on every run that has the door (`crm_account.name` on all five runs; `crm_case.case_number` on B and C, inconclusive on the REST-only A with the reason), 0 contradicted over 13 fields, the inconclusive four carrying the app's own refusals. The evidence came from direct runs of the family, not from `os verify`; see ③.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/15953-verify-unique-scope-family.md`: `@objectstack/verify` **minor**, `@objectstack/cli` **minor**. The diff publishes three new functions and eleven new types from `@objectstack/verify` and one new opt-in flag plus help text from `@objectstack/cli`; it removes and renames nothing, narrows no accept set and changes no default. Minor is the right level for both and meets the card's own acceptance ("`@objectstack/verify` minor per new exported family"). Not breaking, so no migration text and no ADR-0087 disposition marker is owed; `Check Changeset` on the head is green.

`Clause-②` carriers: PR body line 2 `Clause-②: yes`; the changeset body `Clause-②: yes`; the claim comment `6125131626` `Clause-②: yes` (the bare form claim lines take). The three agree. Each is legal: `yes` with no arm is a complete declaration (the `(widening)` arm would add nothing), and `yes` takes at least minor, which both entries are.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev report `6127784027`: `open_questions` is empty, so nothing to answer there. Its deviations and findings, each answered or escalated:

- **The attribution twin** (PM mechanism assumption 2 falsified by measurement): a per-organization refusal names no field because the constraint is the ADR-0120 D3 COALESCE expression index and `uniqueViolationColumn` never reports an index as a column, so "proved only on the code naming the probed field" would prove no per-organization field at all. The twin is the right differential and is pinned. Answered in ①, with the composite residual ESCALATED: the seat owes it a carrier, a follow-up card naming the shape and the one-line tightening above; it does not move this head.
- **Second-organization provisioning** (assumption 3): no sibling family provisions an organization; this one reuses `signUp` and the platform's own workspace door, and addresses the system door by `organization_id` on the row, which the engine requires under a wall. Answered; the changeset's phrasing of it is noted in ①.
- **Walled unit suites booted `multiTenant: 'posture-only'`**: an existing `BootOptions` member on main (harness.ts documents it as the posture without the wall, with real organizations and per-caller stamping), used because no framework package may declare `@objectstack/organizations`. The family's subject is which rows collide, which the index decides from each row's organization, so the posture-only boot measures it; the real-package walled boot is exercised by the hotcrm B and C runs. Answered.
- **The CLI control is a faulted door, not a contradiction**: every config `os verify` loads is `defineStack`-built on a fresh database, so no metadata makes a same-organization duplicate land, and the across leg needs a runtime package CI's graph cannot boot. The two contradiction controls and the attribution control live beside the family. Answered.
- **The positive fixture booted as `defineStack` output**: the parse is what puts the autonumber's `'organization'` on the registered field. Answered, and it is finding 1 below.
- **One conditional surface used** (2 `NOT_A_STAND_IN` rows, the gate red first); the `#22661` `CALLERS` row not needed (the family reads a reference target from the CRUD derivation and never calls `referenceTargetOf`; the core `repo` project is in Test Core, green). Answered in ①.
- **Two merges of `origin/main`** (no conflicts, no force-push): the head is a merge commit whose net diff is the 9 files reviewed. Answered.
- **hotcrm evidence by direct runs, not `os verify`**: this tree is protocol 18 and hotcrm pins `^17.7.0`, so the card's clause "runs from `os verify` on hotcrm's metadata" cannot be met on this tree for this slice either. ESCALATED, not a FAIL: the same open acceptance note slices 1 and 2 landed under (`6116484972`, `6124307791`), the card stays open for its remaining rows, and whoever closes it owes that clause a run or a re-scope.
- **Commit trailers and local leftovers** (the read-only hotcrm clone left in place with a clean tree; the worktree removed): process notes, not contract matters. Answered.
- **Out-of-scope finding 1, `bootStack` over an unparsed literal registers the raw field** (an autonumber that authors no `unique` then gets no index and a system-door duplicate is admitted): ESCALATED as a choice for the seat, not a FAIL. `bootStack` is a public export this README documents (`bootStack(config, opts?)`), `harness.ts` checks no provenance, and the README's examples all pass `defineStack` output without saying it must be; a caller who hands a raw literal with an autonumber gets neither the spec's default nor a refusal. The family itself would report that stack `contradicted`, so it hides nothing, and every CLI door refuses an unparsed stack (`STACK_PROVENANCE_MISSING`). Under #10 this is a note that borders a trap: the carrier is either the provenance refusal on `bootStack` (one card, outside this claim) or one sentence on `bootStack`'s docblock and README line saying the config is `defineStack` output. The seat picks; this PR's fixture is already correct.
- **Finding 2** (the ADR-0120 D3 NULL-organization bucket is unreachable through either door on today's runtime): a statement about what the engine stamps, not a defect; row 7's R residue stays driver-sql's. A note is right. Answered.
- **Finding 3** (`os verify --multi-tenant` with the open `@objectstack/organizations` refuses to boot until a membership policy is declared): by that package's design (`membership-policy-gate.ts`), it applies to `--rls --multi-tenant` alike, and the README now states it beside the flag. A note is right. Answered.
- **Finding 4** (a generic fixture cannot satisfy every app rule, so some hotcrm autonumbers read inconclusive with the app's own refusal): an app fact, reported `inconclusive`, never `proven`. A note is right. Answered.

**Check-runs on the head, read four times in this act, the last just before posting (latest run per name).** At the final read every run had concluded: 34 success, 7 skipped, 0 failure, 0 in progress. Concluded success: `Build Core`, `Build Docs`, `Check Changeset`, `Check Documentation Links`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Flag docs affected by code changes`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` (not governed: no governed path in the file list), the four PR-shape guards, `Spec property liveness`, all six `Test Core` shards, the four `Type Check` jobs, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Lint & Repo Gates`, the eight `Lint ·` jobs and `filter`. Skipped: `Auto Label`, `Check PR Size`, `Console Pin Gate`, the `Dogfood Regression Gate` matrix row, `Dogfood Verify CLI`, `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)` and `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`; the last three and `Console Pin Gate` carry `github.event_name != 'pull_request'` in their own `if:`, so they are roster skips on a PR run, not gates that should have run. No gate was re-run by this act. What the seat owes before the queue: the two carriers named above (the composite-attribution residual, and the `bootStack` provenance choice), each of which is a follow-up outside this diff.
